name: Fleet service planner
summary: Works out which fleet vehicles are due for a service, reads their open device issues for the workshop, and queues a workshop booking for each due service. Crons read and draft; a person approves every booking.

crons.name: status
crons.summary: Read each vehicle's planned services and open device issues into the fleet snapshot.

crons.name: plan
crons.summary: Re-read due services, draft the workshop plan, and queue one booking per due service for approval.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations are reads only. Nothing a cron does reaches the workshop: a booking is a live operation and waits for a person to approve it.

trackunit.covers: planned services per vehicle, open device issues per vehicle, workshop bookings (queued only)

gaps: Approval runs the booking without re-reading the service: approve() only runs live operations, so a read cannot sit in the approval. The plan cron withdraws a pending booking once its service is no longer due, but a service that completes between a plan run and an approval can still be booked. An approval-time recheck needs a core change.
Trackunit: CAN fault reads need a machine id, not the asset id this workflow holds, so active faults are not read yet. Device health issues stand in for defects.
Trackunit: bookings need the planned service id, so a fault with no planned service cannot be booked automatically. The workshop books those by hand.
Trackunit: parts ordering, cost approval, return-to-service and follow-up are not in the vendor docs, so they are not covered.
Trackunit: the access token must be supplied by hand (no token exchange is built). The operations are spec-level and have not run against a live account.
MTData (Talon, Workshop Software): help pages only, with no operation file. Its service triggers, job cards and work orders need a live account and a mapped adapter.
WEBFLEET: marketing and support pages only, with no operation file. Workshop, service and cost steps are not covered.
Call evidence: 2 calls were read and neither described the steps, so the step list and families come from the platform docs, not from owners.

evidence.calls: 2 discovery calls read; 0 steps described by owners
evidence.platforms: Trackunit: 23 mapped operations named in the evidence, 2 reads and 1 booking used here; MTData and WEBFLEET: vendor pages only, no operation files
